audits.title: A completed audit cycle of the lateral scan projection radiograph in CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA); the impact on scan length and radiation dose.
audits.standard: Optimal scan length from lung apex to lung base
audits.setting: Department of Radiology, Bristol Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Mean excess scan length 39.1 mm (SD 20.4) with frontal topogram only.

audits.intervention: Additional lateral topogram in the CTPA protocol and radiographer education.

cycle2.result: Mean excess scan length 19.5 mm (SD 17.4), significantly lower.

audits.other_findings: Dose to liver and stomach significantly reduced; thyroid dose potentially lowered.
audits.citation: Rodrigues JC, Negus IS, Manghat NE, Hamilton MC. A completed audit cycle of the lateral scan projection radiograph in CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA); the impact on scan length and radiation dose. Clin Radiol. 2013;68(6):574-579. doi:10.1016/j.crad.2012.11.016. PMID: 23541095.

audits.title: Multidetector CT radiation dose optimisation in adults: short- and long-term effects of a clinical audit.
audits.standard: Diagnostic reference levels (75th percentile doses) for common CT examinations
audits.setting: All eight multidetector CT departments in Luxembourg

cycle1.result: Baseline survey of CTDIvol and DLP for head, sinus, cervical spine, thorax, abdomen and lumbar spine (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: External clinical audit in each department in 2008 to optimise default CT parameters.

cycle2.result: DLP per examination fell 32-69% for all regions between 2007 and 2009; DRLs reduced by 20-78%, mean DLP per examination by 18-75% and collective dose by 30%.

audits.other_findings: The dose reduction was sustained over time.
audits.citation: Tack D, Jahnen A, Kohler S, Harpes N, De Maertelaer V, Back C, et al.. Multidetector CT radiation dose optimisation in adults: short- and long-term effects of a clinical audit. Eur Radiol. 2014;24(1):169-175. doi:10.1007/s00330-013-2994-8. PMID: 23990004.

audits.title: The usefulness of large sample size patient dose audits for optimisation of CT automatic exposure control (AEC) settings.
audits.setting: Three CT scanners at a single institution (Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: Pre-optimisation patient dose audits (n > 200 per protocol) using RIS data showed sub-optimal automatic exposure control performance on the Toshiba scanner.

audits.intervention: Optimisation of the Toshiba scanner by phantom measurement and investigation of system configuration

cycle2.result: Doses standardised; median dose-length product reduced by up to 43% on the sub-optimal scanner with no adverse effect on image quality.

audits.citation: Moore CS, Wood TJ, Saunderson JR, Beavis AW. The usefulness of large sample size patient dose audits for optimisation of CT automatic exposure control (AEC) settings. J Radiol Prot. 2019;39(3):938-949. doi:10.1088/1361-6498/ab3894. PMID: 31382249.

audits.title: An audit of radiation doses received by paediatric patients undergoing computed tomography investigations at academic hospitals in South Africa.
audits.standard: International paediatric CT diagnostic reference levels (CTDIvol and DLP)

cycle1.result: Most local DRLs compared favourably with international standards, except CT chest and CT abdomen in the 0-1 year age group.

audits.other_findings: DLP was higher after hours at both hospitals, most in the 0-1 year group (150.56% increase); CT brain made up 72.23% of examinations.
audits.citation: van der Merwe CM, Mahomed N. An audit of radiation doses received by paediatric patients undergoing computed tomography investigations at academic hospitals in South Africa. SA J Radiol. 2020;24(1):1823. doi:10.4102/sajr.v24i1.1823. PMID: 33240540.

audits.title: Improving practice in radiology: a quality-improvement project examining CT colonography patient dose and scanning technique.
audits.standard: National diagnostic reference levels for CT colonography (11 mGy CTDIvol and 950 mGy.cm DLP)
audits.setting: 33 imaging protocols across 27 CT scanners in a large UK region; regional dose audit

cycle1.result: Regional DRLs: contrast-enhanced CTDIvol 11 and 5 mGy, DLP 740 mGy.cm; unenhanced 5 mGy and 450 mGy.cm; all compliant with national DRLs.

audits.other_findings: Marked variation in dose and technique between similar scanners; authors suggest the national DRL is too high.
audits.citation: Iball GR, Tolan D, Avery GR, Cope LH, Hoare T, Lambie H, et al.. Improving practice in radiology: a quality-improvement project examining CT colonography patient dose and scanning technique. Clin Radiol. 2021;76(8):626.e13-626.e21. doi:10.1016/j.crad.2021.02.010. PMID: 33714540.
